use_case_name: Resolve Dual Designations via Track Correlation

claims.content: The goal is to prevent or eliminate dual designations of ballistic missile tracks through the process of track correlation.

scope_contract.goal_statement: The goal is to prevent or eliminate dual designations of ballistic missile tracks through the process of track correlation.
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: C2 JU recognizes two tracks being reported to the interface as eligible for correlation and correlates them, so the dual designation is resolved rather than left standing.
scope_contract.start_boundary: C2 JU recognizes that two tracks being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation.
scope_contract.success_boundary: The two eligible tracks have been correlated such that the dual designation is resolved.
in_scope_actions: Recognize that two tracks being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation (EC-G-004)
Correlate the eligible tracks to resolve the dual designation (EC-G-002)
excluded_adjacent_actions: Difference resolution of Environment/Category, Identity, Exercise Indicator, Platform, Platform Activity, Specific Type, and Special Interest Indicator field values (EC-G-003)
Following section protocols to minimize occurrences and duration of dual designations (EC-G-000)
Determining whether automatic correlation is barred by ID conflicts, differing Mode II codes, or Operational Contingency Constraints (EC-G-001)
variant_dimensions: Which track data fields (Environment/Category, Identity, Exercise Indicator, Platform, Platform Activity, Specific Type, Special Interest Indicator) differ between the two designated tracks

claims.content: C2 JU
C2 JU has correlated local sensor data.
All IUs are periodically comparing remote tracks to local tracks (and, optionally, to common local tracks) to determine if a dual designation has occurred.
Two tracks have passed the correlation tests and restrictions twice, satisfying the eligibility requirement for correlation execution.

system state constraints on track attributes
eligibility criteria based on test passage

claims.content: C2 JU recognizes that two tracks being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation.

covered_aspect_ids: specific initiating event for track correlation
specific initiating event or user action for track correlation

claims.content: C2 JU initiates action, either automatically or manually, to resolve the dual designation after recognizing that two tracks being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation.
The process of correlation consists of comparing locally derived sensor data (e.g., position, velocity, boost indication) with the data received on the interface.
When the two tracks pass the correlation tests and restrictions once, they are deemed a tentative correlation.
Upon the next correlation stimulus, the same two tracks are tested again.
When the two tracks successfully pass the second correlation test and there is no correlation restriction, they are processed for dual designation resolution.
C2 JU transmits the J7.2 Correlation message requesting all other C2 IUs to perform a correlation of the two tracks, identifying the track number to be retained and the track number to be dropped.

The receiving IUs accept the requested correlation unless certain prespecified conditions exist which require or allow the receiving IU to reject the requested correlation or respond with a reverse correlation request.

main_flow: initiation of new track report after decorrelation
specify retained/dropped track numbers in message
receiving IUs accept correlation by default

claims.content: Diverges from Step 1: C2 JU may use a manual capability to initiate the correlation of any two tracks irrespective of the correlation test criteria, correlation restrictions, or other correlation requirements.
Diverges from Step 1: Tracks with TQ less than or equal to e are not eligible for correlation, except that new local real-time tracks can still be recognized as eligible for correlation.
Diverges from Step 3: If the speed of either track is less than 10 dmh, the course differential criterion is not applied in the correlation test.

Diverges from Step 5: An exception to the automatic correlation restrictions allows correlation if one track has an ID of Unknown or Hostile and the other has an ID of Friend, permitting the breaking of an engagement or destruction of a missile in flight.
Diverges from Step 6: The J7.2 Correlation message shall not be inhibited by any filter.

Diverges from Step 7: A receiving IU that desires to reverse the requested correlation uses the RV field to determine whether to originate a reverse correlation request; when responding with a reverse correlation, it transmits the J7.2 message with the originally received Retained TN and Dropped TN reversed and the RV field set to value 1.

covered_aspect_ids: alternative_flow: skip course differential test for low-speed tracks
alternative_flow: allow restricted-TQ tracks if new local real-time
alternative_flow: operator alert for conflicting IDs
alternative_flow: exception for Unknown/Hostile vs Friend tracks
alternative_flow: abandonment due to OCC conflict
alternative_flow: partial track hold logic (Retained missing, Dropped present)
alternative_flow: filter inhibition exception for J7.2 message

claims.content: Diverges from Step 2 when the Altitude Source of either track is 0 (No Statement/Estimated) or 2 (Aircraft Report): Altitude shall not be used in the correlation test. Outcome: altitude is excluded from the correlation test.
Diverges from Step 2 when a track has TQ ≤ e: that track shall not be tested for correlation. Outcome: the correlation test is not performed for that track.

Diverges from Step 5 when automatic correlation is attempted and the local/remote data held indicates that both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks (i.e., being updated with local positional data): C2 JUs shall not automatically correlate the two tracks. Outcome: automatic correlation is not performed.

Diverges from Step 5 when conflicting IDs are the only correlation restriction, i.e., an ID difference that cannot be automatically accepted or rejected: the operator shall be alerted and the differences presented for evaluation, with options to (a) change the local ID or Exercise Indicator and ID, allowing automatic correlation; (b) transmit an ID Difference Report, allowing automatic correlation if the remote ID or Exercise Indicator and ID is changed; (c) confirm the restriction, inhibiting the correlation; or (d) conduct voice coordination to resolve the situation. Outcome: operator action determines whether automatic correlation is allowed, inhibited, or resolved via voice coordination.

Diverges from Step 5 when a selection conflict occurs because both the Retained TN and the Dropped TN have an OCC: the correlation shall be abandoned until the next correlation check. Outcome: the correlation is abandoned until the next correlation check.

Diverges from Step 6 after transmission of the correlation request when no J7.0 (ACT = 0) message is received for the Dropped TN within 60 seconds: the correlation is deemed to have failed and all associated processing shall be cancelled. Outcome: the correlation fails and associated processing is cancelled.
Diverges from Step 7 when both the Retained TN and the Dropped TN have an OCC: the correlation shall be rejected. Outcome: correlation is rejected.
Diverges from Step 7 when the two tracks are of a different E/C, or either track has an existing E/C conflict: the correlation shall be rejected. Outcome: correlation is rejected.
Diverges from Step 7 when one track is simulated and the other is live: the correlation shall be rejected. Outcome: correlation is rejected.

Diverges from Step 7 when a correlation request is rejected: the JU shall transmit the J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 to report the rejection. Outcome: the rejection is reported by J7.2 with RV = 2.

Diverges from Step 7 when a correlation request is rejected for a manual correlation: the JU originating the request shall provide an operator alert as a cue to conduct voice coordination. Outcome: the originating JU alerts the operator to conduct voice coordination.

Diverges from Step 7 when a correlation is found with a track for which another C2 JU has R^2 and the TNs are different: the J7.2 (RV = 1) Correlation message shall be transmitted, with the Source TN in the Header word of the J2 PPLI message as the Retained TN and the surveillance TN as the Dropped TN. Outcome: a J7.2 RV = 1 message is transmitted with the specified Retained TN and Dropped TN.

Diverges from Step 7 when a correlation is found with a track for which another C2 JU has R^2 and the TNs are the same: the JU receiving the J2 shall accept the PPLI information into its surveillance database and shall disregard the J3 surveillance data on the specified track, except when Geodetic Position Quality in the PPLI message is set to value 0, in which case the surveillance track is accepted and the PPLI message shall be discarded. Outcome: PPLI information is accepted and J3 surveillance data is disregarded, or when Geodetic Position Quality is 0, the surveillance track is accepted and the PPLI message is discarded.

Diverges from Step 7 when the own unit has R^2 for the Dropped TN: a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message shall be transmitted; if the Dropped TN is reported by another IU after this transmission, the own unit shall retain the Dropped TN as a remote track and shall not reattempt to correlate the Retained TN and the Dropped TN for a period of 60 seconds. Outcome: J7.0 Drop Track is transmitted, and if the Dropped TN is later reported by another IU, it is retained as a remote track with no reattempted correlation for 60 seconds.

missing_aspects: Handling or response when the correlation test does not occur within 6 seconds after the extrapolation time (EC-EF-001).
Documented return-to-step or termination after the voice-coordination option in the conflicting-ID exception branch.
Documented exit or recovery path after a correlation rejection when the evidence only states the rejection or the reporting message.

claims.content: The two eligible tracks have been correlated, resolving the dual designation.
If the own unit held the Dropped TN as a local or common local track, the Retained TN is designated as a common local track upon successful correlation.
If the originating C2 JU holds R^2 data for the Dropped TN, a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message is transmitted for the Dropped TN upon successful correlation.
After acceptance of a manual correlation (RV field set to value 3), the resulting track is not subject to automatic decorrelation processing for 5 minutes.

covered_aspect_ids: postcondition: temporary immunity from automatic decorrelation
postcondition: dropped track removal via J7.0 message
